To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure and dynamics of state building in Africa have been more deeply rooted in rural society than is generally acknowledged.
(a) the state is embedded in local society, (b) state institutions are shaped by conflicts within local society, and (c) the structure of local society is shaped by the structure of the economy.
the structure and politics of the African state at the grass‐roots level are determined by the interaction of the state and the local power structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the political economy of the state and the countryside.
the nature of state formation in the African countryside.
the political economy of state formation and the political economy of rural development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is a major contribution to our understanding of state formation in Africa.
the state in the African countryside is a highly differentiated structure of institutions and relations.
this is the best book on the subject that is currently available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it has shown the state to be a more deeply embedded and locally‐specific institution in Africa than many previous studies suggested, and that this is a key factor in understanding both the successes and failures of attempts to decentralize and democratize in the 1989s and 1999s.
the study is an attempt to understand the political economy of the state and its institutions in Africa.
the book shows that the political dynamics of state building are shaped as much by the politics and social relations of rural society as by the intentions and actions of governments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
state building is not a one-way street from the centre to the periphery.
the state is not a monolith, and its institutions do not operate uniformly across space.
African states are not unitary actors, but rather are made up of a complex array of institutions, some of which are more effective than others.
